steps.text: Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking pan.
In a blender, combine eggs, milk, flour, salt and pepper; cover and process until smooth. Pour into prepared baking pan.
Bake in preheated oven until set, about 20 minutes. Sprinkle with cheese.
Carefully loosen edges of omelet from pan. Starting from the short edge of the pan, carefully roll up omelet. Place omelet seam side down on a serving plate and cut into 6 equal sized pieces.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Omelet Roll
raw_recipe.description: This omelet is so easy and delicious. It bakes in the oven, so there is no watching the stove. My son loves to make it for us.

video.description: No watching the stove with this omelet. It gently cooks in the oven.

review.reviewBody:
Excellent receipe. I failed miserably with the thicker glass pan, even with non-stick spray. I tried again with a 10x15 jelly roll pan, and the results were fantastic. Rolled so much easier! I submitted the photo for this recipe, so you can see how nice it rolled up. 

I'd highly recommend adding whatever typical omelette ingredients you prefer (ham, green peppers, etc). The taste may be a little plain without any -- just like a normal omelette would. I also used sharp cheddar to bring out the cheese taste as well. 

Makes for a very nice presentation, especially compared to how simple it is to arrange. After rolling, sprinkle a little extra cheese and parsley flakes on the top, and it will look very nice.

I made it with changes suggested (cut flour in half; used half water and half 1/2 & 1/2). I had 7 eggs left in the carton, so used all 7. I lowered the oven temp to 400 and baked for 10 minutes, then added bacon, green chilies (squeezed out the excess liquid to avoid sogginess) and shredded cheese and returned to the oven (turned it off) until the cheese melted. I used parchment paper in a jelly roll pan (sprayed the pan and the paper with canola oil spray), which worked very well, and rolled it up on a cutting board to cut it. Served with salsa. I will use more spices next time, and possibly add black olive slices :)

I used a 9 x 13 metal cake pan, so I didn't have to worry about it spilling. Worked well, next time I will definitely line the pan with parchment to aid in the rolling process. I rolled the long side, which I recommend, it ends up longer and you get more slices that way. It would have been easier to roll with the parchment paper lining the pan. My guests loved it, it is very impressive. Also, it's a great way to use up what you have. I used corn, roasted red potatoes and pork tenderloin. (Leftovers from the night before). Chop your add-ins small and don't use too many, you need enough egg surface or it will break when you roll it. Loved it!

Made this for brunch today! Used 1/4 cup flour and added a little salsa to the raw eggs. Baked at 375 used Butter Pam on parchment paper and baked 14 mins., then diced ham, two cups cheese (Taco flavor and Pepper Jack) put back in oven for 3 mins. It rolled so easy (long end) and sliced perfect. This is a dish I want to make over and over and I will for sure!!!! Thank you for this endless ingredients recipe!!

This is really tasty and you can customize it to your own tastes too. I added cooked minced onion to the raw egg mixture and baked, then rolled in shredded cheese and chopped ham to the finished egg. I too experienced the puffed up egg problem while baking the egg in the oven (someone else posted a picture of this problem). I solved this problem by placing a sheet of aluminum foil over the baked egg and gently pressing down the puffed up areas of the egg. Be sure to wear oven mitts for that task!! This is a very formal looking and impressive dish and would be perfect for a brunch gathering. I would suggest some sort of sauce or something drizzled on top of the finished roll (Hollandaise maybe) to give it more pizzazz. I just placed american cheese slices on top and put it back in the shut off (but still warm) oven.

I completely scrapped the baking directions; use cookie sheet lined with parchment paper (where parchment paper comes over the sides) - lightly spray with Pam, bake as per recipe. This is a great base recipe, you can add sautéed onions and mushrooms, diced peppers, or whatever you have handy. Also, if you sprinkle some green onions when you spread the cheese, it gives it a wonderful flavor. When you take it out of the oven, just grab ends of the parchment and roll.

I replaced the all purpose flour with oat flour (for more nutrition), used almond milk (to cut calories), added two cloves of fresh garlic in the blender (for more flavor), after pouring into a parchment-lined pan, sprinkled finely chopped onion, spinach, mushrooms, and fresh tarragon. Added the cheese after baking. The parchment paper is the ticket for rolling. Perfect. Five stars with the changes.

I followed the recipe but used liquid eggs in place of fresh. First batch was too fluffy to roll and served right out of the pan and got raves. Second batch 1 hr later I cut back on the milk and the flour and was able to roll and got raves and request to show how to do it the next time. Lined the bottom of the pan with foil and it helped with rolling. Will be making again because of ease in serving (I got 8)many at once and those served loved it and when they tell mutual friends I will need to do it again.

This is a great basic recipe and turned out very nice. Everyone loved it. I used finely chopped yellow and orange peppers and green onion. I used shredded mozzarella and Colby Cheese and a salt free dilly mix spice just a tad!(that's what I had on hand) I served mini ciabatta rolls and mini sausage patties. Some of my guests made mini sandwiches and some ate theirs separately. I took reviewers advice and used a parchment lined jelly roll pan and sprayed the paper with pam. Next I'm making it with spinach, rumbled bacon, green onion different cheeses. THANK YOU FOR THE RECIPE!!! Oh and again due to reviews I baked at 400 for only 10 minutes it was perfect!

Love this recipe! I altered mine slightly... I baked the omelet for 15 minutes ( instead of 20) @ 400 degrees. I used a dark 13x9 inch pan and had no trouble with sticking like others did. I also added 3/4 bag of frozen veggies along with the cheddar cheese after 15 minutes of baking. Then I rolled the omelet in the same pan and put back in the oven for the remaining 5 minutes. I do agree with a few comments here in regard to the high oven temp. I watched it the whole time in the oven so it didn't burn. I'm extremely happy how the omelet turned out...delish! :)

I liked this recipe, but did a few tweaks, I didn't have any all purpose flour so I uses a little less than a cup of bread flour, and made it kinda like a ham and cheese sandwich scramble, (as I forgot to grease the parchment paper) added ham, onion, tomatoes and a little bit of lettuce, seasoning each layer with a dash of salt and pepper, then baked for 15 minutes, then adding mixed cheese, put back in convection oven for about 1 minute, then turning the oven off for 4 minutes. It came out basically tasting like the omelet I usually make on the stove top but with o whole lot less clean up! I will definitely make this again, as it makes plenty of left overs for quick breakfast in the week! I served it with a couple of hash brown patties and a non-alcoholic mimosa, very tasty! Thank you for sharing this idea!
It’s a quick and easy breakfast. It works best with parchment paper sprayed lightly with olive oil or avocado oil. The parchment paper makes it easier to roll.

I thought I already reviewed but can’t find. Love this with a few small tweaks. I added lots of spices like dill, Italian, garlic, per our preferences. I also left my HEAVILY pan-sprayed foil large around the edges of my cookie sheet. After cooking for about 10 minutes, I rolled the edges of foil over the fluffed up edges of egg to keep them from burning and cooked another 3-5 minutes to finish the center. Came out amazing. Also, rolled from long side to make more manageable rolls. Let it cool just a bit, then used foil to help me roll smoothly and slice. I only had a tiny bit of first one because my boys ate it all!!! You can throw anything in, like most egg dishes, just watch for higher moisture content =longer cook time. We’ve done this several times now, so quick and easy and versatile, different than just “eggs”. Can do a double batch and just halve into pans to save some time, or even do different add-ins on each half of one sheet! Sprinkle some cheese as you are rolling for extra decadence, or spread with sour cream.....,
Use Parchment paper and spray with cooking spray. The paper makes it so easy to roll.

Just made this for brunch. I omitted the flour and substituted 1/4 cup whipped cream cheese and diced brie (just a small slice, cut into tiny chunks). I also added a small amount of finely diced shrimp and scallops, which I sautéed in butter (first draining the buttery juice), and finally, I added shredded extra sharp cheddar cheese. I used a Pampered Chef large bar pan lined with parchment paper. It turned out perfect.

I have actually been making this recipe for years, it is identical to one that was in an old cooking magazine. I don't have the patience to make individual omelets for a family. Also, this one bakes up so much lighter and fluffier than a pan omelet. Feel free to add whatever you want before rolling it up, I like to add chopped bacon and some sauteed mushrooms and onions.

This is a great basic recipe. You can't beat the style of cooking and the way it presents. I followed the directions exactly but made it two different ways on my first attempt. The first batch I made I used a 13x9 inch cake pan, but it really puffed up high. Still great flavor. In the second batch, I used an 11x15 baking sheet which seemed to work so much better. Both tasted amazing and the presentation was beautiful.

Easy to make! I sautéed mushrooms with a few onions in ALDI’s salt-free Table Blend and spread them over the cheese before I rolled it up. Served to guests at the Bed & Breakfast, and they loved how it looked and how it tasted! I can’t wait to try this again with other fillings!

Add 2 egg whites ( 1/4 cp.), reduce milk to 1/2 cup, and reduce flour to 1/4 cup.
This increases protein and decreases fat and carbs. ; also adds extra volume.

This is my “GO TO” recipe when I have a house full of people. I do not roll it up though. I leave it flat and call it breakfast pizza. Kids and adults always request that I make it for breakfast at holiday get togethers. And it’s SO EASY and delicious.
